title: Blood & Bodily Fluids / Sharps Safety
blurb: Handling blood, bodily fluids and found needles safely, and what to do straight away after a needlestick or splash.
siteNotes: Where the bodily-fluid spill kits, gloves and sharps bins are kept
Who to report a sharps find or injury to, and how it is recorded
Where staff get prompt medical advice after a needlestick or splash
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-56. Bloodborne virus risk and the control steps are as the trainer states; employers must assess and control the risk under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and COSHH Regulations 2002.

CHECK: the trainer says to encourage a puncture wound to bleed. Current NHS and UKHSA first aid for a needlestick is to wash with soap and running water, and not to suck or scrub the wound; confirm the venue is happy with "encourage it to bleed gently".

CHECK: the trainer says to use a "tool or a sharps container, or a brush and pan". Confirm the venue procedure for picking up found needles, as many sites ask staff not to handle them at all and to call a trained person.

cards.title: Blood & Bodily Fluids / Sharps Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- protect yourself when cleaning up blood or bodily fluids
- deal safely with a found needle or sharp
- act straight away after a prick, cut or splash

cards.title: What you might come across
cards.body:
In housekeeping and cleaning you can come across blood, vomit, urine or other bodily fluids, and occasionally sharps like discarded needles. These can carry infections, including bloodborne viruses such as hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV.

With the right precautions, the risk is very low.

cards.title: Protect yourself first
cards.body: For any spillage of blood or bodily fluids, protect yourself first. Put on gloves, and an apron and eye protection if there is a splash risk.

items.title: Protect
items.text: Gloves, and apron and eye protection if splashing.

items.title: Disinfect
items.text: Use the correct disinfectant or a spill kit if we have one.

cards.title: Bag it, then wash
cards.body: Double-bag and dispose of waste and used PPE properly. Wash your hands thoroughly afterwards, even though you wore gloves.

left.title: Do
items: Wash your hands, even after gloves

right.title: Do not
items: Skip handwashing because you wore gloves

cards.title: Never with bare hands
cards.body: If you find a needle or other sharp item, in a room, a bin or down the side of a sofa, NEVER pick it up with your bare hands.

items.title: Use a tool
items.text: A tool, or a brush and pan, or a sharps container.

items.title: Sharps bin
items.text: Place it in a proper sharps bin.

cards.title: Act straight away
cards.body: If you are pricked or cut by a sharp, or get blood or fluid into a cut, your eyes or mouth, act straight away.

items.title: Wash
items.text: Wash well with soap and water. Rinse eyes and mouth with water.

items.title: Report
items.text: Report it at once for prompt medical advice.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Blood, vomit and sharps can carry infection, but the risk is very low with precautions
- Gloves first, and apron and eye protection if splashing
- Clean a generous area, double-bag waste and wash hands
- Never touch a needle with bare hands, and report every find
- If pricked or splashed, wash, cover, report and get medical advice

cards.q: Blood and bodily fluids can carry infections such as hepatitis and HIV.
cards.why: They can carry bloodborne viruses such as hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, so they must be handled carefully.

cards.q: You are about to clean up blood in a corridor. What should you put on first?
options: A hairnet and a clean apron over the uniform
Gloves, and an apron and eyewear if splashing
Just a face mask over your nose and mouth
Nothing, as long as you are quick about it
cards.why: Protect yourself first with gloves, and an apron and eye protection if there is a splash risk.

cards.q: You find a discarded needle down the side of a sofa. You should:
options: Pick it up by hand, holding it by the end
Use a tool or sharps container, never bare hands
Push it deeper out of sight in the cushions
Leave it where it is and say nothing
cards.why: Never pick up a needle with bare hands. Use a tool, brush and pan or a sharps container, and report it.

cards.q: You should wash your hands thoroughly even after wearing gloves.
cards.why: Wash your hands thoroughly afterwards, even though you wore gloves.

cards.q: You prick yourself on a sharp. Which is something you should do straight away?
options: Wash with soap and water, cover it and report it
Carry on and mention it at the end of the shift
Put on a plaster and say nothing
Rinse it only if it looks deep
cards.why: Encourage it to bleed a little, wash it well, cover it and report it immediately to get prompt medical advice.

cards.q: Every sharps find should be reported to your manager.
cards.why: Report every find to your manager.

cards.q: When cleaning a bodily-fluid spill you should clean:
options: Only the exact spot
The whole room, top to bottom
A generous area around it
Nothing until it has dried
cards.why: Clean a generous area, not just the exact spot.

cards.q: Used PPE and waste should be double-bagged and disposed of properly.
cards.why: Double-bag and dispose of waste and used PPE properly.

cards.q: With the right precautions, the risk from bodily fluids is very low.
cards.why: With the right precautions, the risk is very low.

cards.q: A found needle should end up in:
options: The general waste bin
The clinical waste sack in the housekeeping store
The nearest recycling bin
A proper sharps bin
cards.why: Place it in a proper sharps bin.
